what_this_is_not: R values are copied from the tracked fixture. Julia values are computed fresh by tools/true_parity_variance_decomp_receipt.jl, which repeats the computation of the cited twin test with the same inputs and settings; R was not run and is not recomputed here.

cases.quantity: extract_proportions(fit), shared_unit proportion of a latent + unique fit at one tier (6 values)
cases.julia_source: GLLVModels.extract_proportions(fit), as called at test/test_variance_decomp_p1.jl:84; fit as at test/test_variance_decomp_p1.jl:78
cases.tolerance_source_line: @test isapprox(extract_proportions(fit), r_sh; atol = 2e-5, rtol = 0)   # shared_unit proportion (observed 2.5e-6)
cases.note: One-tier Gaussian rank-2 fit with a unit-level diagonal, p = 6, 200 units, one observation per cell (sha256 checked); R: latent(d = 2) + unique at unit, converged with a positive-definite Hessian; same optimum (logLik within 1e-6, asserted in the test). R's shared_unit proportion is diag(L L') / (diag(L L') + Psi); the Julia :unit denominator on a has_diag fit with K_W == 0 is the identified total sigma_y_site(fit) (#701), which is the same number because R's Psi absorbs the whole residual. The six R values lie strictly inside (0, 1), between 0.66 and 0.82: not one constant. Replaces the postfit batch case CORE070-ESTIMAND-REBIND-EXTRACT-PROPORTIONS, whose unique = FALSE fixture returned 1 for every trait.

cases.quantity: extract_proportions(fit)$proportion, all four components of a two-level fit (long format, 20 values)
cases.julia_source: GLLVModels.extract_proportions(fit).proportion, as called at test/test_variance_decomp_p1.jl:105; fit as at test/test_variance_decomp_p1.jl:93
cases.tolerance_source_line: @test isapprox(pr.proportion, r_prop; atol = 2e-4, rtol = 0)   # proportion, all four components (observed 2.4e-5)
cases.note: Two-level Gaussian fit, p = 5, 120 units x 4 observations (sha256 checked); R: latent(d = 1) + unique at unit and at unit_obs, converged with a positive-definite Hessian; same optimum (logLik within 1e-6, asserted in the test). R's extract_proportions() long frame has four components (shared_unit, unique_unit, shared_unit_obs, unique_unit_obs) x 5 traits = 20 rows; the Julia TwoLevelFit method returns the same rows in the same order (asserted in the test and again in the receipt generator). The R proportions are 20 distinct non-constant values between 0.02 and 0.45. Limits: Gaussian only, so R's link_residual component (zero for a Gaussian fit) is absent in both.
